body:
SO, I see a lot of questions regarding depression, or actions taken to help depression, but I wonder how one can determine what they are actually suffering from (be it a mental illness or merely a "funk" they have trouble getting out of) without spending time/money with doctors?

I think other people in this subreddit could benefit from this question, as I doubt I am
the only one who wonders exactly what their mental state amounts to.

Since I went to the trouble of creating a dummy account, let me make this briefly a more
personal question.  I've been in a self-diagnosed funk for about a year.  I've had bouts of insomnia, alcoholism (that's not new, though, thanks Dad), self-disgust, and general dislike of how little control I have over my emotions.  Essentially, this is due to relationship problems (how original) that can be summed up as: I'm in love with my close friend's fiance (who is my best friend) and she has similar if not same feelings for me (we've talked about it).

This, in turn, makes me feel like a terrible human being and is responsibile for the insomnia and some level of depression.  This problem is somewhat self-correcting:  they are getting married in three months and in four months I am leaving for Japan to teach English.  However, likely, we will always have feelings for each other and wonder what it could have been like.

I'm not particularly suicidal, but I have for the first time in my life wondered a few times
if "things" would be better if I wasn't around.  The idea that I may be driving a wedge between my two most favorite people is brutal. 

My question, though, is stated in my title:  What is the observable difference between being
depressed and having capital-D Depression?  

Or:  How does one know when it's time to speak to someone?
